title: A full-rank tracer mass balance identifies storage, recharge and evaporation in one changing mixed store
abstract: We test whether a known tracer mass source removes a storage ambiguity in changing water stores. For one fully mixed store, three independent tracer equations identify storage, recharge and evaporation. Streamflow and integrated water balance then give cumulative non-stream export. We prove the rank condition and show that a finite injection does not fix future storage scale after injection ends. An independent synthetic test gives identical flow and tracer records with a 10% later storage difference. In 3,600 noisy simulations, weak injection or weak evaporation contrast makes the inverse estimate unstable despite full rank. One strong virtual design gives a cumulative loss error range of -8.2% to +9.0%; a tenfold smaller injection gives -88.8% to +120.0%. These are simulation ranges, not field uncertainty. The method needs known mass delivery into the observed store, known tracer behavior and complete mixing. It does not identify the cause of Australian runoff loss. Proofs, code, full synthetic results, provenance and an independent audit are included.
